endorsements.quote: Stakeholders, developers, end users, and policymakers need to be collectively, meaningfully, and substantively integrated into all phases of the AI life cycle to realize transparency goals, establish societal trust, achieve health equity, and improve population health.
PAs need to use temporally relevant data sets with meaningful minority representation that do not exacerbate disparities and disparate health outcomes.

To reduce racial bias in health care–related algorithms, we must identify bias at every level of the health care system and society and then identify how these biases are reflected in health care data analytics to reduce racial bias in health care–related algorithms.

unlisted_practices: Integrate industrywide algorithmic vigilance into health care organizational culture to realize health equity goals.
Adopt a national AI health strategy that realizes the Quintuple Aim and minimizes race-based medicine.
Include social determinants such as job security, housing, and education in algorithm development.
Use legal definitions of harmful bias, distinguishing disparate treatment from disparate impact, to define and categorize algorithmic bias.
Retain and reuse missing data in AI datasets for comparison rather than discarding them entirely.
Obtain informed consent and take care in how data are collected for AI development.
Staff AI development teams with professionally diverse members, including end users, and center patient voices in algorithm design.
